lines.text: Which parameters of your model fit your data best?
The ones that minimize the error, or make your data most probable.
This is an optimization problem.
Picture the error as a landscape: the lower the ground, the better the fit. You want the lowest point.
But you can't see the landscape. Each evaluation gives the height at a single point.
Bayesian optimization fits a surrogate to the points it has seen: a statistical model of the whole landscape.
It evaluates where the ground looks low, or might be. Then it updates the surrogate, and repeats.
When the surrogate is accurate, this is smart and fast.
But the surrogate can be wrong. If the landscape has a shape it can't capture, it keeps pointing to the wrong places.
Instead, direct search uses no surrogate.
From the best point so far, it tries a step in each direction, on a grid called the mesh.
If a step finds lower ground, it moves there and takes bigger steps. If none does, it takes smaller ones.
It can't be fooled, and it comes with convergence guarantees. But it is slow.
Bayesian Adaptive Direct Search, or Bads, combines the two.
lines.caption: Bayesian Adaptive Direct Search, or BADS, combines the two.

lines.text: It alternates a search stage, Bayesian optimization around the best point, and a poll stage, a round of direct search.
lines.caption: It alternates a SEARCH stage, Bayesian optimization around the best point, and a POLL stage, a round of direct search.*

lines.text: As long as the search finds better points, Bads keeps searching. When it fails several times in a row, Bads polls.
lines.caption: As long as the SEARCH finds better points, BADS keeps searching. When it fails several times in a row, BADS polls.

lines.text: The two stages help each other.
When the surrogate fails, the poll moves away from the region it can't model, and the points it collects help build a better surrogate for the next search.
lines.caption: When the surrogate fails, the POLL moves away from the region it can't model, and the points it collects help build a better surrogate for the next SEARCH.

lines.text: Here is a real Pie-Bads run, on the same landscape.
lines.caption: Here is a real PyBADS run, on the same landscape.

lines.text: It starts with a few evaluations and fits the surrogate. The search heads downhill fast.
lines.caption: It starts with a few evaluations and fits the surrogate. The SEARCH heads downhill fast.

lines.text: But the trench is too narrow for the surrogate. From one deep point, it predicts deep ground where there is none, and four searches in a row fail.
So Pie-Bads polls. One step lands in the trench, far lower than any point before, and the mesh grows.
lines.caption: So PyBADS polls. One step lands in the trench, far lower than any point before, and the mesh grows.

lines.text: The points from the poll show the surrogate the shape of the trench.
lines.caption: The points from the POLL show the surrogate the shape of the trench.

lines.text: Now the search is fast again: its next point lands near the bottom of the trench.
lines.caption: Now the SEARCH is fast again: its next point lands near the bottom of the trench.

lines.text: When no step improves any more, the mesh shrinks, and Pie-Bads settles on the minimum.
lines.caption: When no step improves any more, the mesh shrinks, and PyBADS settles on the minimum.

lines.text: Pie-Bads never saw the true landscape. Here it is.
lines.caption: PyBADS never saw the true landscape. Here it is.

lines.text: Smart and fast when the surrogate is right. Slow but steady when it's wrong.
That landscape had two parameters. Bads works with up to twenty, on rugged or noisy landscapes.
lines.caption: That landscape had two parameters. BADS works with up to twenty, on rugged or noisy landscapes.

lines.text: On dozens of real model-fitting problems, it matched or beat sixteen other optimizers.
lines.caption: On dozens of real model-fitting problems, it matched or beat sixteen other optimizers.*

lines.text: Since then, it has been used in hundreds of studies, from brains and board games to oil wells and wildfires.
lines.caption: Since then, it has been used in hundreds of studies, from brains and board games to oil wells and wildfires.*
